tasks.short: Revisit land users and record implementation observations.

steps.what: Retrieve implemented plans and previous visit findings
Travel to the land user's implementation site
View implemented land practices against the plan
Record observations, photographs and departures from implemented plans
Discuss observed implementation and next actions with land users

tasks.design: Configure a site-indexed native view and visit form in {DOCS}. The scientist observes the implementation, writes the record and communicates findings; the form only reduces reference searching and repeated headings.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans and earlier observations must be found and copied into another visit record.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document links and reusable visit fields can retain site context.
tasks.still_hard: Visible practice may differ from actual long-term performance.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise site-specific departures and discuss workable corrections.
tasks.altitude: Give the scientist more time to compare field conditions with the plan.

reach.learn: Use the same site identifiers and distinguish observation from interpretation.

evidence.claim: Native site folders and visit templates could reduce retrieval and repeated record preparation; this is an unmeasured task scenario.

assumptions: The baseline includes travel, viewing, the visit record and discussion; none is excluded.

The scientist produces site identifier, visit date, plan version, observed practice, photograph references and departures in s4; its retained time includes capture. Missing fields stay narrative and require manual completion.
Try native document views and forms before building an application. No new automated action or separate save is proposed.
The 30% record reduction concerns headings and repeated site details, not interpreting observations.
unknowns: How much visit record preparation is repeated today?
research_questions: Does the native form reduce writing time without losing departures and uncertainties?

already_counted.description: Scientist captures and checks the visit record.

incremental.description: Maintain site links and the visit form.

approvals.approved_version: The exact findings and next actions expressed to this land user; new advice is checked before it is spoken.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 scenario: B=100, R=93.5, gross saving=6.5; 1.5 upkeep gives central net=5. Range is below that estimate.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inspect erosion sites, record evidence and identify causes or solutions.

steps.what: Retrieve erosion history and site reference material
Visit areas affected by erosion and inspect terrain
Measure erosion features and inspect possible contributing processes
Write the erosion field record with measurements and photographs
Identify erosion causes and document suitable solutions and uncertainty

tasks.design: Use a native site reference view and erosion field template in {DOCS}. Keep field measurement and causal assessment with the scientist, including the written recommendations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Site material and repeated field record structure consume preparation and recording time.
tasks.enabler_now: Linked folders and reusable field templates can carry site identifiers and headings.
tasks.still_hard: A short visit may miss rainfall, drainage and land-use processes responsible for erosion.
tasks.human_edge: Combine physical evidence with uncertainty and practical intervention constraints.
tasks.altitude: Make the evidence behind each proposed erosion solution easier to inspect.

reach.learn: Link measurements and observation dates to the same erosion site.

evidence.claim: A native site view and field record template could reduce clerical preparation without replacing erosion diagnosis; the saving is unmeasured.

assumptions: Travel and inspection are in s2; measurements in s3; the record and written assessment are separately counted in s4 and s5.

The scientist produces location, date, measurement units, measured values, photo references and observation caveats in s4. Its retained 10.5 hours include capture; incomplete observations remain explicit rather than becoming defaults.
Use native document links and templates first. No sensor integration, model inference or machine write is assumed.
Written causal reasoning remains fully manual; the record saving only concerns repeated structure and details.
unknowns: Whether field records already use an efficient template.
research_questions: What time is spent on repeated field headings versus new scientific observations?

already_counted.description: Capture the erosion evidence and check units and photograph references.

incremental.description: Maintain reference links and field template.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 scenario: B=100, R=93.5, gross=6.5; upkeep=2 gives central net=4.5. Existing good templates could erase the gain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare and provide conservation information or training to government agencies.

steps.what: Clarify agencies' water or soil management questions
Select evidence and specify conservation advice or learning objectives
Draft agency information notes or training materials

loop.purpose: Draft explanatory material from selected evidence.
loop.input: Scientist's advice outline and identified source passages.
loop.output: Draft material with source references and explicit gaps.
loop.check: Scientist checks each substantive statement and relevance to the agency's situation.
loop.stop: One revision; unsupported passages are written manually.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates provide structure but cannot assemble varied explanatory prose.

steps.what: Check the agency materials against evidence and intended advice
Send the final conservation materials to the agency
Provide expertise and training, adapting explanations to agency questions
Record agency questions and agreed coordination actions

tasks.design: Use a native outline and session template in {DOCS}, then a bounded drafting loop for explanatory prose. The scientist selects evidence, checks the final material, sends it through {EMAIL}, delivers the training and records coordination actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Explanatory material is repeatedly drafted for different agency contexts.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft can use a selected source pack rather than inventing technical advice.
tasks.still_hard: Advice must fit local water and soil conditions and agencies' responsibilities.
tasks.human_edge: Translate uncertain science into usable explanations and coordination agreements.

ambition.what: Reuse checked explanatory modules for another agency without weakening site-specific advice.

tasks.altitude: Shift preparation effort toward evidence and practical agency questions.

reach.learn: Supply dated observations and limits for the scientist's source pack.

evidence.claim: Source-bounded drafting and native session templates could reduce preparation work; this agency-training saving is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: The task includes written material, its real send, training and subsequent coordination record; each phase has a step.

The scientist produces needs in s1 and source passages, citation identifiers and advice outline in s2. The loop accepts only that pack; missing support is drafted manually. Capture time remains fully counted.
Native templates and reusable checked modules come first; the loop only handles variable prose.
The s4 internal edit has no self-approval gate. Recipient and exact final attachment are checked during the real send.
unknowns: Share of agency support that requires new written training material.
research_questions: Does drafting from the selected pack reduce preparation after factual checking and corrections?

already_counted.description: Review and correct the generated draft.

incremental.description: Maintain checked source modules and test drafting quality.

approvals.approved_version: Exact final material version and agency recipient; attachment edits or recipient changes require another send-time check.
Checked material and each new live answer; the scientist verifies applicability before communicating advice.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 scenario: B=100, R=89, gross=11; incremental upkeep=3 gives central net=8. Range reflects variable preparation needs.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Enter validated environmental data into decision tools and assess suggested analyses.

steps.what: Collect local soil, water and environmental input data with provenance
Map environmental values and units to decision tool fields
Enter the mapped environmental input batch into the decision tool
Run the decision tool's configured analyses on accepted inputs
Check entered values, import exceptions and analysis output validity
Identify appropriate analyses or techniques and note limitations

tasks.design: Use a native import mapping from {SPREADSHEET} into an internal decision tool in {OPS_SYSTEM}. Separate data entry from running the analysis; retain source capture, exception handling and scientific selection of appropriate techniques.
tasks.previous_blocker: The scientist rekeys measured values into a second tool and starts repeated runs manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Stable field specifications and supported batch import can remove actual rekeying.
tasks.still_hard: An apparently valid numerical result can be unsuitable for the local soil or water question.
tasks.human_edge: Check measurement meaning, model assumptions and practical applicability.

ambition.what: Evaluate another input scenario using the same validated source table.

tasks.altitude: Spend less time transferring values and more time testing applicability.

reach.learn: Record units, location, sampling date and method with every value.

evidence.claim: Supported field mapping and batch import can remove rekeying into a decision tool; the proposed labour reduction is an unmeasured E1 scenario.

assumptions: Baseline really contains a separate manual data transfer and repeated run initiation. Existing automatic calculations earn no additional saving.

The scientist produces site identifier, coordinates, sampling date, measurement method, variable, value, unit and quality caveat in s1; all capture remains counted at 25. Mapping choices are produced in s2. Missing or incompatible fields stop import for manual correction in s5.
The decision tool is an internal private analysis workspace; this task does not publish or send results outside the organisation.
Try native import and saved analysis settings first; no agent or inferred environmental measurements are required.
The input commit is the explicit s3 action; there is no extra time claim for a same-system save. Running the tool is separately counted in s4.
unknowns: Whether the actual tool supports import and repeatable run initiation.
How many input fields currently require manual rekeying.
research_questions: Does a supported import preserve units and missing-value meaning on a held-out set of local records?

already_counted.description: Check imported values, resolve exceptions and validate outputs.

incremental.description: Maintain mappings and regression-check imports after tool changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 transfer-and-run scenario: B=100, R=57, gross=43; upkeep=8 gives central net=35. Lower range allows import limitations and a smaller rekeying baseline.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retain field observation and scientific interpretation while reducing repeated documentation and data transfer.
reach: Coordinate field evidence with conservation technicians and agency counterparts.
role.ambitious_version: A conservation scientist who links field observations, traceable records and practical advice without delegating causal judgement.
